probes.desc: Correct answer written as a CTE (WITH clause)
probes.note: Clause-level analyzer has no WITH grammar; parser rejects or misreads.

probes.desc: Correct answer using a window function instead of GROUP BY
probes.note: Window functions are outside the shape grammar; outcome depends on filter.
USING is executable; join extraction regex expects ON - may degrade shape info.

probes.desc: Correct answer via derived table in FROM
probes.note: Derived tables parse loosely; filter should accept on equivalence.

probes.desc: Function call renames output column (comma inside args)
probes.note: Pins the F2 repair. The comparator used to key on column NAMES, so the same data under a renamed header was judged non-equivalent and this probe returned DEGRADED; it now keys on values in column order, and the renamed header no longer diverges. What is left is a LATENT case of the F4/F5 kind: COALESCE differs from the bare column only on a NULL-bearing instance, and the fixture's artist.country has none. A return to name-keying would show up here as DEGRADED again. Exposing the residual difference is a job for instance construction, not for the comparator.
Quoted identifiers must not confuse the clause splitter.

probes.desc: Uncorrelated EXISTS where reference uses IN (documented gap)
probes.note: M9 rule anchors on reference shape (base must be EXISTS/NOT EXISTS); wrongness is caught by execution only - no misconception label. Confirmed at corpus scale in Phase 3.2 (0/2).

probes.desc: WHERE predicate weakened (wrong literal), not dropped
probes.note: M1 fires only on MISSING where-clause; wrong-literal errors have no misconception category - execution divergence is the only signal.

probes.desc: Extraneous join multiplying duplicate rows (student adds a table)
probes.note: Was a double blindness when first discovered: MISSING_JOIN covers too-few tables only (too-many has no category), AND the set-semantic result comparison was duplicate-insensitive, so row multiplication was judged output-equivalent and the query passed as alternate-correct. The F4 multiset repair closed the second half - the duplicate rows now diverge. The first half stands: a too-many-tables error still yields no misconception label, so the student is told the query is wrong and nothing more. Wrong, undiagnosed - which is what makes F3c a residual family worth probing.

probes.desc: LEFT JOIN wrong shape, output-equivalent under full FK coverage
probes.note: Every artist has an album in the fixture: outputs match, filter suppresses WRONG_JOIN_TYPE. Quantified at scale in Phase 3.2 (153/191 LEFT-join corruptions latent). Raw flag retained for research.

probes.desc: NOT IN over subquery that can yield NULL (three-valued logic)
probes.note: Fixture album.artist_id has no NULLs: outputs match (latent). The division corpus catches this class via NULL-injected edges.

probes.desc: UNION ALL instead of UNION (duplicate semantics)
probes.note: Set-comparison of results is duplicate-insensitive; UNION-vs-UNION ALL divergence is invisible unless the branches overlap. Detector normalizes ' ALL' away by design.
